notes: STATUS partial: the Central Mediterranean is covered for 2023-2025 from a primary IOM/UNHCR document; the whole Mediterranean (2023, 2025), the Atlantic route (2025 and Sep 2024-May 2025), Bay of Bengal/Andaman Sea and the Caribbean are covered only partly, and the Eastern and Western Mediterranean routes are not covered at all. The portal's route-by-year dashboard is JavaScript-rendered and all iom.int press pages refused the fetcher, so IOM's own 2025 route table was never read directly. COUNTING RULES (IOM methodology page): the Project records people who die during migration toward an international destination, at external borders or in transit, whatever their legal status; deaths in immigration detention, after deportation, in camps or housing, and of internally displaced persons are excluded. 'Number dead' is left blank where migrants are missing and presumed dead, as in shipwrecks; 'Number missing' is the number reported aboard minus bodies recovered minus survivors, usually from survivor or witness accounts, and is blank if none reported. Every incident carries a 'Source quality' score 1-5 (1 = one media source; 5 = official sources such as coroners or multiple humanitarian actors); IOM and UNHCR coordinate validation in the Mediterranean. IOM states all figures are minimum estimates and 'remain undercounted'. INVISIBLE SHIPWRECKS: not a term in the methodology. IOM officials use it for shipwrecks with no survivors (UN News 2021), which are 'nearly impossible to verify'. No IOM numeric estimate of unrecorded deaths was found anywhere opened; IOM's GMDAC portal says only that most migrant deaths go unrecorded. The '1,500' that press (and the ledger) attach to 2025 is IOM's count of additional people REPORTED missing at sea whose cases could not be verified and are excluded from the totals; it is recorded as migrants-unverified-missing-at-sea-2025 and labelled as such, not as an estimate.
